items.stem: Explain any four functions of commercial banks.
items.answer: (i) Acceptance of deposits: Banks accept deposits in current, savings and fixed deposit accounts. (ii) Lending of funds: Banks lend through overdraft, cash credit, loans and discounting of bills. (iii) Cheque facility: Cheques let customers make payments safely without handling cash. (iv) Remittance of funds: Banks transfer funds from one place to another through drafts and electronic transfers. (v) Allied services: Bill payment, lockers, underwriting and buying or selling securities for customers.

items.stem: Explain any four characteristics of entrepreneurship.
items.answer: (i) Systematic activity: It needs knowledge, skills and competencies that can be learnt. (ii) Lawful and purposeful activity: It is undertaken within the law to create value and earn profit. (iii) Innovation: It creates new products, processes or markets. (iv) Organisation of production: The entrepreneur brings together land, labour and capital. (v) Risk-taking: The entrepreneur bears the risk of the business.

items.stem: Explain any four methods of payment in online transactions.
items.answer: (i) Cash on delivery: Payment is made when goods are delivered. (ii) Cheque: A cheque is sent to the seller, who delivers after it is cleared. (iii) Net banking transfer: The buyer transfers money to the seller's account online. (iv) Credit or debit card: Card details are given online and the card account is charged. (v) Digital cash: Electronic currency is used for payment.

items.stem: Explain any four elements of business ethics.
items.answer: (i) Top management commitment: The CEO and top managers must lead and be openly committed to ethical conduct. (ii) Publication of a code: A written code lays down principles such as fairness, honesty and quality. (iii) Establishment of compliance mechanisms: Systems such as careful hiring, training and reporting ensure the code is followed. (iv) Involving employees at all levels: Employees at every level must take part in ethics programmes. (v) Measuring results: Ethical performance must be monitored and audited, though it is hard to measure exactly.

items.stem:
Verma Industries wants full control of its operations in a large foreign market and has ample funds.
(i) Which mode of entry suits it? (ii) Give two merits and two limitations. (iii) How would a joint venture differ?
items.answer: (i) Wholly owned subsidiary. (ii) Merits: full control, no sharing of profits or secrets. Limitations: high investment, full risk, not suited to small firms. (iii) Ownership, investment and risk are shared with a partner, who also brings local knowledge.
